headline: 111 dead as 7.4 magnitude earthquake hits Colombia
summary: A powerful quake struck western Colombia, collapsing buildings in several cities and leaving dozens trapped under rubble as the new administration declares a state of emergency.
details: At least 111 people were killed and 87 others injured after a powerful 7.4 magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia early yesterday.
According to the US Geological Survey, the quake hit at a depth of 107km near San Jose del Palmar in Choco, a sparsely populated province on the Pacific Coast, though it was felt nationwide.
The disaster has thrust the new administration of President Abelardo De La Espriella into its first major crisis just days after he was sworn in.
President De La Espriella has declared a national state of emergency, stating that the first priority is rescuing those still trapped under the rubble.
In the city of Cali, Mayor Alejandro Eder reported that more than two dozen structures collapsed, leaving people trapped and requiring disaster teams from Bogota and Medellin.
In Manizales, a tower of the city's cathedral fell over and numerous buildings sustained damage, causing traffic paralysis and fear of aftershocks.
Choco Governor Nubia Carolina Cordoba-Curi reported significant damage and injuries in the provincial capital, Quibdo, while warning residents about potential aftershocks.
caption:
111 dead and dozens trapped as a massive 7.4 magnitude earthquake devastates western Colombia.

At least 111 people were killed and 87 others injured after a powerful 7.4 magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia early yesterday.

According to the US Geological Survey, the quake hit at a depth of 107km near San Jose del Palmar in Choco, a sparsely populated province on the Pacific Coast, though it was felt nationwide.

The disaster has thrust the new administration of President Abelardo De La Espriella into its first major crisis just days after he was sworn in.

President De La Espriella has declared a national state of emergency, stating that the first priority is rescuing those still trapped under the rubble.

In the city of Cali, Mayor Alejandro Eder reported that more than two dozen structures collapsed, leaving people trapped and requiring disaster teams from Bogota and Medellin.

In Manizales, a tower of the city's cathedral fell over and numerous buildings sustained damage, causing traffic paralysis and fear of aftershocks.

Choco Governor Nubia Carolina Cordoba-Curi reported significant damage and injuries in the provincial capital, Quibdo, while warning residents about potential aftershocks.

headline: Over 5 lakh fail as SSC pass rate hits 19-year low
summary: Pass rate across 9 general education boards dropped to 64.05%, with English and Mathematics identified as the primary causes for the decline.
details: The pass rate for the SSC examinations across nine general education boards has fallen to 64.05%, the lowest in 19 years. Out of 1,404,539 students who appeared for the exams, 899,610 passed while 504,929 failed.
caption:
Over 500,000 students failed their SSC exams this year, marking the lowest pass rate in nearly two decades.

The pass rate for the SSC examinations across nine general education boards has fallen to 64.05%, the lowest in 19 years. Out of 1,404,539 students who appeared for the exams, 899,610 passed while 504,929 failed.
